title: Ophthalmic Trauma & Infections: Clinical Mastery Guide
summary: A comprehensive clinical reference for the diagnosis, classification, and management of penetrating eye injuries, ocular surface disorders, pterygium, and infective keratitis. This guide integrates diagnostic protocols with evidence-based management strategies for residents and fellows.

sections.title: Penetrating Eye Injury: Assessment & Classification
sections.content: A 38-year-old man with no previous ocular history reports irritation of his right eye after doing some work around the house. On exam, the patient has 20/20 vision and normal intraocular pressure. A1: Colour anterior segment photograph focused on Iris shows iridotomy, with no past ocular history possibility of an IOFB is more likely the culprit although, no corneal opacity or entry site can be seen in this photograph. A2: Ask a detailed history (hammering, sawing, power tools), use of eye protection. Obtain orbital CT, B-scan or X-ray. AVOID MRI if metallic IOFB is suspected.

rows: Glass, plastic, sand, stone, ceramic, gold, platinum, silver, aluminum
Must be removed; high risk of endophthalmitis/toxicity
Sunflower cataract, Kayser-Fleisher ring, green iris
Heterochromia, mid-dilated pupil, yellowing cortex, vitritis

sections.title: Ocular Surface Stains & Dry Eye
content: Fluorescein: Dry eye, Seidel's test, NLD patency, Tonometry, FFA, Contact lens fitting.
Lissamine Green: Dry eye (Sjogren's), lid wiper epitheliopathy.
Rose Bengal: Conjunctival staining, dry eye, neoplasms (dysplastic cells), herpetic dendrites, MGD.
Trypan Blue: Anterior capsule (capsulotomy), DSEK (stripping Descemet's), DALK (endothelium stripping), Tenon's capsule, ERM.
Indocyanine Green: Anterior capsule, ILM visualization, Choroidal circulation/PCV/AMD diagnostics.
Triamcinolone Acetonide: During PPV / anterior vitrectomy.
Brilliant Blue G/Acid Blue/Bromophenol Blue/Patent Blue: ILM/ERM staining.

sections.title: Infective Keratitis: Mycotic Ulcer Trial
content: MUTT 1: Natamycin 5% vs Voriconazole 1%. Natamycin is superior for filamentous fungi; Voriconazole should NOT be monotherapy for Fusarium.
MUTT 2: Oral Voriconazole had no overall benefit in advanced fungal keratitis except potentially in Fusarium cases.
Side effects (Antifungals): Gastrointestinal (nausea/vomiting), liver enzyme changes, skin irritation, visual disturbances.

sections.title: Red Flags & Clinical Pearls
content: NEVER use MRI if metallic IOFB is suspected.
Fungal Hypopyon: Convex upper border, low mobility, yellow color.
Bacterial Hypopyon: Concave upper border, mobile, white color.
Antimetabolites (Mitomycin C) complications: Necrotizing scleritis, sterile melts, calcification, delayed healing.
Fungal Keratitis: Persistent epithelial defect, satellite lesions, 'fuzzy' borders.
